question: A user has connected the Gmail connector and asks Claude to reply to a client email. What happens once Claude has drafted the reply?
options: A) Claude holds the message for a workspace administrator to approve before anything leaves the account
B) Claude sends it straight away, because authorising a connector authorises every action that connector offers
C) Claude can send it, but by default it asks the user to approve the action before the message goes out
D) Claude can only produce a draft, because a mail connector is limited to searching and reading messages
correct_answers: C) Claude can send it, but by default it asks the user to approve the action before the message goes out
explanations: The approval prompt goes to the person making the request, not to an administrator. Administrators control whether a connector is available at all, not individual messages.
Authorising a connector does not hand over unattended permission to act. Write actions are gated by an approval step by default, which is the point of that design.

Correct. Sending, replying and forwarding are write actions the mail connector supports, and by default Claude asks for approval before each one. The user stays in control of what actually leaves the account without having to copy the draft out by hand.
Mail connectors are not read-only. Alongside searching and reading, they support sending, replying to and forwarding messages.
